- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. - claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). input.reason: Verified in source: write_csv (messreihe_report_exporter.hpp:52-56) streams variant_name/engine strings raw without any quoting/escaping; variant_name = phase.name + "@" + op_label (v32_messreihe_antrieb.hpp:173) where phase.name is a verbatim XML attribute (xml_config_parser.cpp:394) and op_labels are whitespace-split tokens (xml_reader.hpp:44-54) — commas survive both. validate_experiment_profile (validate_profile.hpp:444-551) checks phase.merge/engines/registries but never phase.name charset and never op_types. The XSD constrains op_types (OP-1..OP-6) but leaves phase name as unconstrained xs:string, and the XSD is enforced nowhere (no xmllint/schema validation in code or CI) — so even a schema-valid XML with a comma in phase name silently shifts all following columns. The consumer test (test_v32_messreihe_antrieb.cpp:129-137) checks only header equality + row count, so a shifted row passes undetected. Not documented design; conflicts with the canon's fail-loud/honest-measurement doctrine (the validator's own docs name silent XML typo classes as its target). Minor corrections: axis_id is compile-time-safe (not XML-driven), and the op_types half is weaker than claimed since the XSD nominally forbids commas there — phase.name is the proven vector. Latent (golden XML uses safe names, driver INERT-by-default) but silent data corruption in the thesis-feeding measurement CSV: med is correct.
